<!-- All news items below this line -->{{Current events|year=2003|month=11|day=4|content=
* The U.S. [[National Cancer Institute]] is funding human [[clinical studies]] to test experimental [[reovirus]]-based [[cancer]] treatments, after initial studies show promising results against a number of different types of tumor which contain the Ras [[oncogene]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.oncolyticsbiotech.com/what.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031205030923/http://www.oncolyticsbiotech.com/what.html |archive-date=2003-12-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bloodjournal.org/cgi/gca?sendit=Get+All+Checked+Abstract(s)&SEARCHID=1048034467148_12950&JOURNALCODE=&FIRSTINDEX=0&hits=10&RESULTFORMAT=&gca=2002-02-0503 ]{{dead link|date=October 2015}}</ref>
* [[War on Terrorism]]: In [[Saudi Arabia]], an attempt at a terror attack on Saudi officials, pilgrims, or both, in the holy city of [[Mecca]] is foiled; plotters believed to be linked to Al Qaeda.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=3751356 |title=World News |publisher=Reuters.com |date=2009-02-09 |accessdate=2015-10-24 |archive-date=2004-12-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041208155925/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=3751356 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[American occupation of Iraq|Occupation of Iraq]]: For the second night running the HQ of the coalition in central Baghdad comes under attack; huge explosions are heard.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3241785.stm |title=Middle East &#124; US vows to improve Iraq security |publisher=BBC News |date=2003-11-05 |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref> Spain, one of the staunchest supporters of the US in the Iraq war, withdraws many of its staff from its embassy in Iraq.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lasvegassun.com/sunbin/stories/w-me/2003/nov/04/110404366.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930035222/http://www.lasvegassun.com/sunbin/stories/w-me/2003/nov/04/110404366.html |archive-date=2007-09-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Whilst the [[Sri Lankan prime minister]] [[Ranil Wickremesinghe]] is visiting the United States, the country's president [[Chandrika Kumaratunga]] suspends parliament and deploys troops, effectively putting the country into a state of [[martial law]].
* The [[Anglican Church]] splits over [[gay bishop]]. Half the archbishops of the Anglican union denounce the [[Episcopal Church in the United States of America|Episcopal Church]]'s consecration of the world's first openly gay, [[Gene Robinson]], non-celibate bishop and vowed not to recognize the appointment.<ref>{{cite web|author=By |url=http://www.washtimes.com/national/20031104-120602-5953r.htm |title=Archbishops condemn 'choice' - Washington Times |publisher=Washtimes.com |date= |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref>
* The [[sun]] surprises astronomers by launching [[2003 Halloween solar storms|another solar flare]], this time the largest ever recorded.
* Software company [[Novell]] has announced that it will purchase [[Linux distribution|Linux distributor]] [[SUSE S.A.|SuSE]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.novell.com/news/press/archive/2003/11/pr03069.html |title=Press Releases |publisher=Novell |date= |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.suse.com/us/company/press/press_releases/archive03/novell_suse.html |title=Linux OS &#124; SUSE Linux Enterprise |publisher=Suse.com |date=2014-11-17 |accessdate=2015-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031205034045/http://www.suse.com/us/company/press/press_releases/archive03/novell_suse.html |archive-date=2003-12-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* A study in Germany shows that [[leech]]es can help with [[arthritis]] pain, apparently because their saliva contains anti-inflammatories.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=healthNews&storyID=3751996 |title=Health & Fitness News |publisher=Reuters.com |date=2009-02-09 |accessdate=2015-10-24 |archive-date=2004-12-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041210044329/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=healthNews&storyID=3751996 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A59399-2003Nov3.html ]{{dead link|date=October 2015}}</ref>
* [[Mark Messier]] of the [[New York Rangers]] scores two goals against the [[Dallas Stars]], giving him 1851 to pass [[Gordie Howe]] and to move into second place on the [[National Hockey League|NHL]] career points list.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dallas/sports/topstories/stories/110503dnspostarslede.1c53aad9.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041210025952/http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dallas/sports/topstories/stories/110503dnspostarslede.1c53aad9.html |archive-date=2004-12-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[Mexico|Mexican]] President [[Vicente Fox]] begins a three state trip to the United States with a stop in [[Arizona]], where he addresses immigration issues. A man is reportedly injured at a shooting near the place Fox spoke.<ref>http://aolsvc.news.aol.com/news/article.adp?id=20031104215209990005</ref>
* Canadian author [[M.G. Vassanji]] is awarded the [[Giller Prize]] for his book ''The In-Between World of Vikram Lall''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbc.ca/stories/2003/11/04/giller_vassanji031104 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060225092310/http://www.cbc.ca/stories/2003/11/04/giller_vassanji031104 |archive-date=2006-02-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=ManagingTeam |url=http://www.honestreporting.com/articles/critiques/Something_Fishy_at_AFP.asp |title=Something Fishy at AFP |publisher=honest reporting |date=2003-11-04 |accessdate=2015-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081123011522/http://www.honestreporting.com/articles/critiques/Something_Fishy_at_AFP.asp |archive-date=2008-11-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In [[Ecuador]], [[Angel Shingre]], a [[Peasant|campesino]] leader and human rights campaigner who played a key role in bringing to light environmental problems caused by oil exploration in Ecuador's Amazon region, is assassinated in the city of [[Puerto Francisco de Orellana|El Coca]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Name: * |url=http://www.greenleft.org.au/current/561p18d.htm |title=Sorry, we couldn't find that page &#124; Green Left Weekly |publisher=Greenleft.org.au |date= |accessdate=2015-10-24 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
